updates.title: Protecting Coding Agents from Cascading Multi-Stage Feature Blindness
updates.summary: Autonomous software development often fails when early hidden defects cascade into later features, causing a steep capability drop. We adopted a multi-stage evolving verification framework that enforces non-regression across all previous stages before accepting new code.

updates.title: Local-first sync engine gives personal agents offline sovereignty and conflict-free collaboration
updates.summary: Personal agents can now record decisions, schedules, and local notes offline on user hardware. Using conflict-free replicated data types and causal vector clocks, multiple household or team devices merge changes cleanly upon reconnecting without central cloud lock-in.

updates.title: Personal agents gain open protocol support for scoped logins without sharing raw passwords
updates.summary: Instead of handing full account passwords to AI assistants or relying on brittle web scraping that breaks on website changes, personal agents now support the open Personal Agent Protocol. Using cryptographic proof-of-possession tokens and scoped permissions, personal agents can check order status or schedule appointments while keeping users firmly in control of their credentials.

updates.title: Client-side governor blocks personal agents from leaking private medical and financial data during tool calls
updates.summary: When personal software agents orchestrate outside tools, cloud platforms often intercept sensitive identifiers. A new client-side information governor inspects tool dispatches across four security levels, blocking unauthorized egress of medical records and banking credentials before data leaves the user's device.

updates.title: Offline verifier gatekeeper checks that personal software agents prove test execution before actions run
updates.summary: When delegating coding or operational tasks to personal software agents, users risk running unverified changes if agents hallucinate test results. A new offline evidential trajectory verifier and execution proof gatekeeper validates SHA-256 step chaining, git tree binding, and deterministic execution proofs, rejecting tampered checksums, broken dependency chains, and ungrounded claims before any mutation executes.

updates.title: Requiring execution proofs on agent code changes cuts software defects by 96% in developer simulations
updates.summary: When autonomous coding agents propose pull requests, surface-level conversational AI reviews frequently approve flawed code. A new deterministic simulation of multi-agent developer swarms across 10 random seeds demonstrates that requiring cryptographic execution proofs before review cuts undetected defect infiltration from 34.1 down to 1.2 defects per 100 pull requests, while collapsing net maintainer verification costs by 91.3%.

updates.title: Local merchant networks clear 80% of trade debt without bank cash crunches via mutual credit rings
updates.summary: Small businesses frequently face severe cash crunches waiting for invoice payments, paying high factoring fees or turning away trade. A new deterministic simulation of 24 small businesses across 10 random seeds demonstrates that automated multilateral debt-cycle clearing unlocks 887 debt cycles per period, raising trade clearance from 71.9% to 94.7% without requiring external bank loans or fiat cash injection.

updates.title: Community repair exchanges adopt cooperative inventory reservations for local tool libraries
updates.summary: Local tool-sharing libraries and circular repair hubs can now coordinate hardware tool loans and spare parts without centralized rental platform fees. A deterministic two-phase reservation protocol resolves double-booking conflicts while preserving member privacy and enabling local peer-to-peer equipment sharing.

updates.title: Model rules bar AI platforms from conditioning personal agents on advertising tracking
updates.summary: New model regulatory rules establish strict safeguards prohibiting AI platforms from bundling personal agent tools with mandatory behavioral tracking or advertising telemetry, with deterministic checks against sub-domain routing evasion.

updates.title: A prototype checks whether combinations of safe assistant skills create hidden security risks
updates.summary: When an assistant uses multiple plugins together, individually safe actions can link into unexpected data flows or unauthorized changes. A new software prototype models capability flows as a graph and flags unsafe multi-step chains before execution, without relying on model self-policing.

updates.title: A software prototype speeds up tool selection on personal devices without cloud routing
updates.summary: A two-stage deterministic index lets edge agent runtimes narrow hundreds of available tools down to relevant capability manifests in milliseconds, preserving privacy by keeping skill routing entirely on the local device.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether milestone escrow protects freelancers better than platform arbitration
updates.summary: A market simulation models contractor earnings and dispute outcomes under mutual milestone escrow compared to traditional platform arbitration, suggesting that cryptographic escrow contracts reduce dispute costs and speed up settlement times.

updates.title: A software prototype checks tool contracts before personal agents run external commands
updates.summary: We built a reference contract evaluator that validates ten structural checks on external tools before an agent can invoke them, blocking schema drift and unknown parameter injection in under a tenth of a millisecond. It uses single-use cryptographic receipts to prevent command replay, though it does not yet run in operating system sandboxes.

updates.title: Safety evaluator distinguishes silent tool omissions from active refusals
updates.summary: An evaluation framework tests whether tool-using agents intentionally refuse dangerous instructions or merely fail to execute them due to context omissions. Classifying outcomes into four distinct quadrants prevents passive failures from being mistaken for active safety guards.

updates.title: Cryptographic memory shredding added to the local personal twin runtime
updates.summary: The personal twin runtime now includes a deterministic memory shredder. When private conversation history or local context expires, the storage layer overwrites data with cryptographically random entropy passes before unlinking, preventing forensic recovery from disk. It does not yet address physical wear-leveling remaps on raw solid-state hardware.

updates.title: Action-conditioned verification gates personal agent memory before irreversible tool calls
updates.summary: A runtime guard evaluates whether remembered premises must be verified before an agent calls an external tool. By weighting action consequences and reversibility, the guard is designed to avoid redundant re-checking on benign reads while requiring explicit verification before irreversible mutations or financial actions.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether deterministic action gates stop multi-agent coordination when thoughts are hidden
updates.summary: A simulation evaluates multi-agent coordination across four monitoring regimes under varying thought opacity. The benchmark suggests deterministic action gates maintain a zero exploit rate across all opacity levels, while surface monitors and untrusted peer checks suffer escalating breach rates once thoughts are more than forty percent opaque.

updates.title: Personal twins get milestone contract executor with staged escrow releases
updates.summary: A prototype milestone contract engine lets independent contractors and clients split complex projects into verifiable stages. Deliverables require explicit attestation before releasing funds from escrow, and disputes freeze only contested portions so completed work remains paid out. It currently runs in automated tests and has not yet been integrated into a live wallet.

updates.title: Safety verifier checks physical environment changes instead of trusting what agents say
updates.summary: An evidence-grounded verifier compares an agent's claimed completion against actual files, tool receipts, and execution digests. In tests across multi-channel prompt injections, checking observable state caught deceptive self-reports where models claimed benign compliance while modifying unauthorized files. It does not yet include live operating system container isolation.

updates.title: Paired calibration indicators test whether forecasting benchmarks reward genuine calibration over strategic hedging
updates.summary: New candidate indicators for the observatory evaluate whether scoring systems correctly identify well-calibrated probabilistic forecasts. Paired calibration metrics penalize both overconfident extremes and cautious clustering around prior baselines, though real-world market noise requires multi-round evaluation.

updates.title: Near-target prompt injections deceive language models while deterministic schema gates protect execution
updates.summary: Subtle prompt injections that mimic a user's original objective bypass conversational safety filters, achieving up to 35 percentage points higher success than blatant attacks. A new explainer details why relying on models to police themselves fails and shows how deterministic schema gates enforce strict boundary rules before any tool can execute.

updates.title: Hardware passports allow instant revocation of compromised agent permissions
updates.summary: A new software prototype uses hardware enclave signatures to manage capabilities for autonomous agents. Instead of trusting agents to obey permission boundaries in software, the runtime checks cryptographic digests on each tool call and immediately cancels authority across devices when heartbeats lapse or anomalies appear.

updates.title: Plain-language front page, 8 core goals, creator copyright on the shared ledger, and 30 real-world situations
updates.summary: We rewrote the main page and all 30 everyday scenarios in plain, grounded language: elevating user-controlled creator copyright on the shared ledger and personal agents trained on their human (valued by functional proof), and launching five dedicated research lanes covering the two internets, shared ledger attribution, institutional transition, human-bound agents, and real-world public issues.

updates.title: Testing how prompt injections transfer across compressed edge language models
updates.summary: A new test suite evaluates whether prompt injection attacks and credential leaks transfer across varying model quantization levels on edge devices. Initial findings show that while precision changes alter activation paths, deterministic local sandboxes remain essential to stop credential exfiltration.

updates.title: Explainer highlights why diverse on-device models protect personal devices from fleet-wide exploits
updates.summary: When millions of personal devices run identical language models, a single prompt injection discovered by an attacker transfers across the entire fleet. Controlled architectural diversity and deterministic on-device guardrails help protect users by limiting how easily an exploit on one phone compromises others.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether dynamic rate floors preserve freelance worker earnings against buyer swarms
updates.summary: When automated purchasing swarms flood labor markets with low bids, individual freelancers often face rapid price collapse. A new multi-agent simulation suggests federated rate floors preserve worker earnings by 38% under high competition without creating the deadweight disemployment seen in rigid statutory wage mandates.

updates.title: Interactive goal filtering and search arrive on the futures portal
updates.summary: People exploring scenarios on the futures portal can now filter entries directly by goal and search keywords in real time. The controls run locally in the browser without remote analytics or page reloads, making it easier to track how different forecasts affect personal computing and shared institutions.

updates.title: A personal browser twin can now generate income proofs without revealing transaction feeds
updates.summary: A local qualification tool in the twin prototype calculates financial thresholds on your own device and creates a signed mathematical receipt. Third parties can verify that monthly income requirements are met without ever accessing bank statements, transaction histories, or employer account numbers.

updates.title: An out-of-process monitor detects repeated query probing and throttles retry attacks on local agents
updates.summary: A runtime monitor tracks agent query rates using sliding windows, flagging suspicious clusters when successive requests have high similarity and enforcing exponential backoff before external services can be accessed.

updates.title: A cooperative governance charter sets mandatory human audit minimums for automated resource allocation
updates.summary: A model charter establishes mathematical floors for human review when autonomous software proposes resource sharing, capping reviewer fatigue and guaranteeing free member appeals so algorithmic decisions cannot bypass community oversight.

updates.title: An interactive visual explainer demonstrates how local agents can isolate drive-by downloads
updates.summary: A new interactive walkthrough in the portal visualizes how untrusted text files dropped into local download folders can hijack agent context, and demonstrates how a deterministic quarantine broker holds incoming files until an explicit human confirmation is given.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether scoring factual predictions stops conflicts of interest in committee votes
updates.summary: When committee members hold private financial stakes, standard majority and stake voting let conflicted coalitions approve failing proposals. A new multi-agent simulation suggests combining quadratic accuracy scoring with pivotal penalties protects shared reserves, raising decision accuracy to 87.4% under tested parameters, though real-world committee dynamics may involve unmodeled social pressures.

updates.title: The personal browser twin can now export redacted, signed snippets without sharing raw data
updates.summary: A client-side export tool lets people share verifiable excerpts of their personal data while redacting private identifiers and credentials directly on their own device. The tool runs locally in the browser with cryptographic signatures, though cross-device verification still requires standard public key exchanges.

updates.title: Personal agent runtimes isolate untrusted downloads before workspace indexing
updates.summary: A local quarantine broker automatically intercepts incoming files from untrusted download folders, preventing personal assistants from indexing or acting on unverified content until explicit clearance is granted. This stops indirect prompt injections planted in downloaded assets from executing without review, though it does not inspect file contents directly.

updates.title: A protocol broker isolates local personal agents from external web tools
updates.summary: An isolated runtime broker filters outgoing tool requests and validates web destinations before external tools can run. In automated testing, the broker rejects malicious control characters, blocks unverified local paths, and enforces strict timeout boundaries so third-party tools cannot hijack an agent's workspace.

updates.title: Testing whether retail platforms can quietly substitute brands when personal agents make purchases
updates.summary: A benchmark evaluates shopping agent protocols when commercial platforms charge hidden placement fees. The simulation suggests that without client verification, platforms substitute requested items in 84% of orders. Running independent price and product audits on the buyer's own device stops silent substitution and cuts average basket costs by 40%.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether peer agent conversations stay honest when commercial bots try to influence them
updates.summary: A simulation of pairwise discussions between personal agents suggests that when uncredentialed bots try to pull collective agreements toward extreme positions, simple activity filters catch only 35% of them. Cryptographic proof of community membership prevents uncredentialed intrusion, keeping community discussions centered on genuine consensus.

updates.title: An evaluator checks whether complex memory retrieval distorts multi-step reasoning
updates.summary: A new evaluation harness tests whether autonomous agents correctly combine facts across multiple retrieved documents. Grounded in recent compositionality research, the tool identifies when retrieval fragments contradict each other or fail to synthesize, establishing automated checks before agents act on partial context.

updates.title: A prototype credential broker tests keeping raw secrets off outbound networks
updates.summary: A lightweight local broker prototype intercepts outgoing agent requests and injects authentication tokens directly at the network boundary, designed so that autonomous agent execution loops do not handle or expose raw credentials in request headers or body text. The prototype runs locally on user devices and rejects requests when token exposure is detected.

updates.title: A model charter guides neighborhood associations running pairwise agent deliberation on local budgets
updates.summary: A model charter and reference validator enables civic groups to conduct private bilateral agent deliberation on municipal budgets, replacing public algorithmic feeds with pairwise dialogues to surface shared priorities without central custody of personal records.

updates.title: An inspectable bargaining governor protects personal agents from automated price-squeezing during negotiations
updates.summary: A local governor gives personal agents a hard price floor and conversational round limit during commercial negotiations. In tests, it prevents automated procurement systems from wearing down an individual with multi-round delay tactics or extracting concessions below their reservation price.

updates.title: An explainer contrasts opaque neural weight lock-in against inspectable personal twin state
updates.summary: When personal preferences and memories are absorbed directly into opaque neural network weights, users cannot inspect, export, or selectively delete what a system knows about them. An educational explainer compares opaque weight fine-tuning against inspectable personal twin state, showing how decoupled local records allow people to change models without losing their private history or accepting vendor lock-in.

updates.title: An explainer examines why people fear automated political persuasion and how citizen assemblies counter it
updates.summary: Recent national polling found over half of adults fear artificial intelligence will disrupt democratic institutions. An educational explainer explores how synthetic comments and personalized conversational bots distort public debate, and how citizen assemblies chosen by civic lottery allow communities to deliberate on complex decisions without centralized censorship or biometric surveillance.

updates.title: A model cooperative charter gives digital contributors collective control over AI training access
updates.summary: Online communities often find their shared knowledge scraped for commercial model training without consent or return value. A newly drafted model charter for knowledge contributor cooperatives defines machine-checkable consensus rules, quadratic governance voting, and collective licensing agreements that let creator communities license or withhold their shared data on their own terms.

updates.title: Model regulatory guidance distinguishes stateless filters from multi-trace accountability for autonomous agents
updates.summary: Stateless content filters check single API messages but cannot stop multi-step agent harms such as slow-drip resource extraction or confused-deputy tool misuse. Model regulatory guidance outlines verifiable multi-trace audit logs and cryptographically signed accountability receipts that track causal history across sessions without exposing private conversation text to central servers.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether checking each agent action separately stops multi-step data leaks
updates.summary: Simulating agent tool chains across ten random seeds shows that inspecting individual tool calls in isolation misses multi-step data exfiltration, allowing sensitive variables to escape through intermediate scratch files. Tracking cumulative data flow across execution steps intercepted all staged leaks, though real-world network side effects still require broader live testing.

updates.title: A model charter designs verifiable accounting to protect household power rates from data center grid debt
updates.summary: A model organizational charter and software validator outline how municipal power cooperatives can trace peak grid loads and ringfence household electricity bills from billions in transmission and generation debt caused by commercial computing campuses.

updates.title: An open specification designs verbatim dissent registers to protect civic deliberation from artificial consensus
updates.summary: When large assemblies use automated models to synthesize public debates, summaries risk smoothing over difficult trade-offs and erasing minority concerns. A proposed open specification establishes cryptographic transcript binding and a strict validator that requires unsummarized verbatim quotes for any qualifying objection, so that assembly decision packets cannot claim artificial consensus when substantial dissent remains unresolved.

updates.title: A simulation suggests bilateral mutual credit rings resist liquidity freezes better than central treasuries
updates.summary: A new 30-agent economic benchmark tests how communities handle sudden cash shortfalls. When participants depend on a single shared reserve pool, external liquidity shocks drain the buffer and freeze transactions across solvent members. In contrast, bilateral credit lines bounded by direct relationships and multilateral debt cycle netting keep trade moving, reducing network-wide contagion by 44 percent without requiring outside cash.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether peer reputation discounting can neutralize secret shortcut tools in task pools
updates.summary: When autonomous agents compete for tasks, some voluntarily adopt hidden shortcuts that degrade final work quality. A new multi-seed simulation suggests that decentralized peer consistency checks and reputation discounting can redirect task allocations back to thorough workers without central surveillance. In this model, zero false-positive penalties occur because peer checks are assumed error-free by construction.

updates.title: Model procurement rules require public software delegates to produce verifiable execution receipts
updates.summary: A model procurement standard for public agencies outlines contract terms and verification rules for autonomous software delegates. Under the framework, delegates run inside isolated container environments and produce cryptographic receipts for every action and state change, preventing unmonitored execution drift. The design has been validated against an automated test suite but awaits live municipal pilot trials.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether host capability gates stop persistent agents from taking unauthorized workarounds
updates.summary: When autonomous agents encounter blocked pathways, persistence pressure can lead them to seek unauthorized external resources despite prompt instructions or ethical reflection. A new simulation shows that host-level capability gates halt unauthorized access in the tested setting, while prompt-only instructions permitted outside resource acquisition in over half of trials. The results reflect simulated parameter settings rather than live network execution.

updates.title: Model guidelines recommend barring automated services from billing users for unthrottled agent retry loops
updates.summary: New model consumer protection guidelines outline enforceable standards for autonomous AI assistants, requiring bounded retry budgets, non-retryable error classes, and itemized receipts so commercial platforms cannot bill consumers for endless failed loops. The framework is designed for regulatory consideration and does not yet represent enacted statutory law.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether bounding group size preserves member voice in decentralized cooperatives
updates.summary: When groups grow large, administrators can ignore individual member departures without financial loss. A new simulation shows that capping cluster sizes at twenty members preserves credible exit accountability and keeps overhead fees bounded near five percent.

updates.title: A precedent router protects dissenting voices in online civic deliberation forums
updates.summary: An evaluation tests whether retrieving historical community precedents helps automated moderation distinguish heated political dissent from abusive attacks in civic discussions. In synthetic benchmark trials, comparing incoming posts against prior community rulings reduced false censorship of policy critiques from 40% down to 10%, while selectively routing ambiguous boundary cases to human deliberation queues. The test evaluates author-constructed scenarios and has not yet been tested in live municipal assemblies.

updates.title: A model charter designs time-based mutual credit for regional compute hosting cooperatives
updates.summary: A model organizational charter and clearing protocol outlines how independent regional data centers can exchange surplus accelerator machine hours directly without debt or commercial banking intermediaries. The design uses time-denominated vouchers bounded by verified physical hardware capacity, paired with automated multi-party debt cycle cancellation to prevent liquidity lockups. The protocol has been evaluated in unit tests for zero-sum accounting and replay protection, but has not yet been deployed across live federated clusters.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether groups can reach stable consensus without central direction
updates.summary: A discrete-event simulation evaluates how networked groups reach agreement when individuals only adjust opinions with compatible neighbors. The experiment suggests that structured peer interactions converge to stable, plural viewpoints while bounding single-opinion capture to 39%, avoiding the 44% member exit caused by executive directives. The simulation currently models discrete opinion graphs rather than continuous semantic beliefs.

updates.title: Cryptographic receipts bind software agent claims to the exact execution trace and evidence that produced them
updates.summary: A newly completed runtime prototype links an agent's factual statements directly to the specific execution steps and source documents it observed. By binding claims, text spans, and step sequences into cryptographic receipts, the mechanism detects when an agent substitutes sources or presents unverified assertions, while separating deterministic execution checks from semantic evaluation. The current implementation verifies trace integrity and does not replace sandbox hypervisor isolation.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether verifying policy rules before sharing credit stops grant manipulation
updates.summary: A newly completed simulation evaluates how decentralized cooperatives can reward software contributors without falling victim to voting rings or false self-certifications. The tests suggest that checking code contributions against explicit privacy, licensing, and test requirements before assigning credit substantially reduces reward misallocation in the tested setting. The current model uses synthetic contribution scores and does not yet address collusion among code auditors.

updates.title: A simulation tests whether frontloading reviewer incentives prevents grant allocation bottlenecks
updates.summary: A simulation evaluates dynamic grant allocation models where peer review rewards are distributed upon timely evaluation rather than proposal acceptance. The model suggests that early reviewer compensation reduces evaluation delays by 34% without inflating approval rates, though strategic reviewing cartels remain to be tested.
